study_identification.author_journal_year: Ge et al., Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification.title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

study_characteristics.study_objective: To empirically benchmark normative modelling algorithms for brain morphometry and identify the optimal approach and covariates for robust lifespan models.

clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: MFPR with nonlinear age terms and linear global measures outperformed alternatives for regional brain morphometry normative modelling; models showed strong accuracy across the lifespan, stability within age bins, longitudinal stability over ~2 years, and performance gains plateauing beyond ~3,000 participants.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using 37,407 healthy individuals (53% female, aged 3–90 years) from 87 datasets, eight algorithms (OLSR, BLR, GAMLSS, LMS, GPR, WBLR, HBR, MFPR) were benchmarked. MFPR emerged as preferred, optimised with non-linear polynomials for age and linear effects of global measures (ICV, mean CT, total SA) as covariates. Training used 5-fold CV within sex-specific training sets with 80/20 train/test splits stratified by site and age. Performance was excellent across the lifespan and within distinct age bins, with longitudinal stability demonstrated over ~2 years. Performance improvements plateaued at cohort sizes >3,000 participants.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Under-representation of some age ranges (young and middle-aged adults) and limited long-term longitudinal follow-up; generalisability to specific ancestries remains to be tested; potential additional explanatory variables (e.g., childhood adversity, preterm birth, SES) were not included and could both improve performance and constrain applicability if required across datasets.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: CentileBrain web portal provides pretrained optimal parameters for application to user-specified datasets; comprehensive comparison included site-handling strategies (ComBat-GAM vs HBR), suggesting practical advantages of ComBat-GAM for harmonisation without per-site calibration.

general_notes.general_notes: Journal: Lancet Digital Health 2024; 6: e211–21. Sex-specific models across 150 morphometric measures (68 CT, 68 SA, 14 subcortical). Site handling compared via HBR random effects vs ComBat-GAM; sensitivity analyses found no support for HBR superiority in this context. CentileBrain portal (https://centilebrain.org) hosts pretrained parameters and scripts.
